card.intuition: MCP is a standard protocol for plugging external tool servers into a harness, giving an agent tools beyond what the harness ships with. The agent never calls MCP directly - it calls a tool, and the harness happens to have gotten that tool from an MCP server.
card.analogy: A standard USB port for tooling: instead of building a custom cable for every device, one protocol lets any MCP-compatible harness use whatever server implements it.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next - MCP changes where tools come from, not the round-trip structure.
card.space_complexity: Every advertised tool arrives as a full definition - name, description, parameter schema - so a few generous servers can burn thousands of tokens on schemas before anything is typed.
when_to_use: When the agent needs tools from an external system like Linear or Slack without hand-writing custom wrappers
When you want one integration written once and usable by any MCP-compatible harness
When enabling servers, enable only the ones a project actually needs to control the up-front token cost
gotchas: The naive approach loads every tool definition into the context window up front, spending attention budget on tools the task never uses
The model can only call tools it knows about - if a definition never arrives, the tool is invisible to it
If your harness doesn't offer tool search, the up-front cost applies and grows with each server you install

steps.label: Expose
steps.annotation: An MCP server advertises the tools it offers, following the standard protocol.

steps.label: Connect
steps.annotation: The harness connects to the server and its tools become available to the agent.

steps.label: Load
steps.annotation: Each tool arrives as its definition, and the model can only call tools it knows about.

steps.label: Call
steps.annotation: The agent never calls MCP; it calls a tool the harness happened to get from the server.

exercise.prompt: Simulate a harness caching a tool definition from an MCP server the first time it is needed. Once known, the definition stays available even if the server drops it.
hints: The first request pulls the definition from the server into the harness's cache
Definitions are loaded lazily - only the tools the agent actually reaches for
